concept.name: Lower low
concept.definition: A swing low that breaks below the previous swing low. Together with lower highs, a sequence of lower lows constitutes the structural definition of a downtrend.
concept.intuition: Each drop undercuts the last floor, showing sellers keep gaining ground.
concept.mechanics: Identified by comparing successive reaction troughs: when the latest decline trades or closes below the prior trough, a lower low is printed. In an uptrend, a newly printed lower low is conventionally read as the first structural warning of a possible trend change.
concept.failure_modes: Lower lows are often produced by stop-driven flushes that immediately recover; a marginal undercut does not by itself confirm a downtrend.
concept.misconceptions: That a lower low in an uptrend proves the trend has reversed; it is a warning sign within a sequence, not a verdict.
concept.example: A stock falls to 88 after previously bottoming at 90, printing a lower low that extends the downtrend's structure.
